title: Chronic persistent hepatitis is usually diagnosed when someone does a liver biopsy
content: Chronic persistent hepatitis is usually diagnosed when someone does a liver biopsy on a patient that has persistently elevated serum transaminases months after a bout of acute viral hepatitis, or when someone is found to have persistently elevated transaminases on routine screening tests. The degree of elevation (in the serum transaminases) can be trivial, or as much as ten times normal. Other blood chemistries are usually normal. As a rule, patients with CPH have no clinical signs of liver disease.
